Executive Summary The adoption of advanced energy technologies is happening to varying degrees around the world and has the potential to enhance energy security and resilience; however, these technologies can introduce new vulnerabilities even as they mitigate existing ones. This dichotomy highlights that both action and inaction carry strategic risks in a contested and logistically complex operating environment. Regardless of U.S. civilian or military adoption of such technologies, key allies and adversaries are on adoption paths that will impact the U.S. military at the tactical, operational, and strategic level. The global adoption of advanced energy technologies presents the potential for both positive and negative consequences for U.S. Department of War (DOW) (also referred to as the U.S. Department of Defense) missions in the next 10–20 years.
